### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**12** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **67** of **249** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **6** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4ab1218901d7c3c757217c099f06d377e04ae452` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `d39bf6673afa0ce21e2985436e2ffdc8acc0818a` — the merge of head `8a83eed2d557a0bde918b4d55746ba08f10a7bc6` into base `4ab1218901d7c3c757217c099f06d377e04ae452`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin d39bf6673afa0ce21e2985436e2ffdc8acc0818a && git checkout d39bf6673afa0ce21e2985436e2ffdc8acc0818a
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 4ab1218901d7c3c757217c099f06d377e04ae452 8a83eed2d557a0bde918b4d55746ba08f10a7bc6 && git checkout -B drift-repro 4ab1218901d7c3c757217c099f06d377e04ae452 && git merge --no-ff 8a83eed2d557a0bde918b4d55746ba08f10a7bc6

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4ab1218901d7c3c757217c099f06d377e04ae452
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## 席位核对 — REWORK (PR body only) · head 8a83eed2d557a0bde918b4d55746ba08f10a7bc6

No code change is asked for. The code, pins and gates hold, as listed below. Two Acceptance-notes residuals name no carrier, although one exists.

### To fix (body edit; the head stays 8a83eed2d5)

1. **"Same family, not in this PR (class a, user-visible): the decision door's refusal remedy and the submitter's `approval.comment` notice … still name the machine name"** and **"Observation (class a, user-visible): the `{{who}}` hole carries the approver type's English machine token in every pack"**. Both are user-visible residuals, and neither line cites a `#N`.
   - #36308 (open) covers both: "the decide refusal and the submitter notice still name a no-approver position by its internal name, and the approver-type word stays English in every pack".
   - Cite `#36308` on each line. An out-of-scope residual with no `#N` is a REWORK item even when its card exists.

A body edit re-runs the PR-body guards. Tell me when they are green, and I will read the body alone.

### Checked and holding

- **Shape:** `l1-face.mjs --pr 36306` is clean at 8a83eed2d5, with 40 success, 15 expected skip, 0 failed and mergeable_state clean.
  - `Fixes #36035` is right: To-do 1 to 3 and the acceptance line are met, and the type word is outside "label, never the name".
  - The declarations are `Clause-②: no` · `Metadata-protocol: none`, and the changeset is a patch on `@objectstack/plugin-approvals`. Nothing is governed, so the area lands it.
- **Store and read (`no-approver-note.ts`):**
  - **Write:** a new note stores `slots`, the slate's `type:value` literals, with the same filter `noApproverWho` used: no platform-admin address, and colon-bearing only.
  - **Stored audit text is byte-identical:** the row's `comment` is still `noApproverNoteText(note)` with no render. `noApproverWho(slots)` with no label composes `type 'value'` exactly as before.
  - **Read:** `noApproverNoteOf` accepts both shapes. A malformed `slots` (not an array of strings) is rejected whole, and an old `who` note is rendered as stored. `positionLabel` is applied only when a `render` is given, so the English never carries a label.
- **Labels (`approval-service.ts`):** `localizeRoutingNotes` resolves `noApproverPositions(note)` through #36030's `notePositionLabels`, the same chain the administrators' note uses: pack label `positions.<name>.label`, then the declared `label`, then the name. `slatePositions` is a byte-identical extraction from `adminRescuePositions`, which now calls it.
- **Pins (#35418's shared harness):** 5 cases.
  - The snapshot stores the slot while the row stores the English with the name.
  - zh-CN reads the pack label and never the name.
  - A pack with no translation (`ja`, `en`) reads the declared label.
  - A position with no label keeps its name.
  - The CONTROL: an old `who` note renders exactly as before.
  - The report's ablations each turn a case red, and each restore was proven against HEAD.
- **Docs:** `approvals.mdx` gains one sentence (label for a reader, name in the stored text), which is true at this head.
- **Remedy path:** the decide-door refusal at `approval-service.ts:5886` still composes `noApproverWho(pendingApprovers)` with no labels. It is not a stored note, and #36308 carries it (item 1).
